note: A genuinely two-sided set: the habitual beat over its own cut guide plus a near-doubled short base and live sale speculation (i0, i2) against persistent Asian port congestion and post-Aug-5 peer EMEA weakness (i1, i3), so the lean is slight and the 12.9% implied move is mostly uncovered by evidence.

Rests on i6 and i4: a reaction function that bought 6 of 7 prints (including a Q1 miss WITH a guide cut) and a tight +/-4.5% move history, against +14.5 points of put skew, 13% short and a stock already 35% off its high — plus comp arithmetic nobody's preview does (Q4 laps -4.8% with a 53rd week), which is why the FY midpoint survives a weak Q3 comp; the rates/Lowe's/Sherwin macro negatives are real but have had three months in the tape.

i0 is the one document-backed, quantified, company-level number in the whole pack — the company's own 10-06 IR Volume & RPC file puts Q3 options RPC at $0.098 against the $0.103-0.11 management told the street to model, implying ~$127-128M of revenue against a published $131.9-135.4M consensus that still carries pre-Oct-6 numbers — but it is heavily discounted by i2: four brokers cut targets in the three weeks after that file and the stock is 6.7% off its 52-week low after a -9.9% week, so most of the direction is already in the tape even though the headline comparison is not.

The unpriced item is i5 — $1.95bn of authorisation left (17% of market cap) with Q2 buybacks at only $79m after $1.94bn in Q1 and a fresh undrawn $700m revolver, so a stepped-up pace announced with results is new — plus i4's de-risking (-10.8% in 5 sessions, -4.8% on the day, calls bid); i0's habitual beat of the top of its own guide is capped hard because this name sold a 2.3% beat for -8.68% and a top-of-guide print for -21.76%, and i2 (company-confirmed EU cross-border drag reaching a +25% Q4 comp) with i6 (a three-day-old CFO setting his first guide) are the offsets on the line that decides this stock.

i6 carries it: +28.9% in 20 days and +10.1% in 5 into a name whose three 2026 beat-and-raises were all sold (-17.26% on the one with the identical run-up), open interest almost entirely calls (put/call 0.03) while the skew still pays for downside, and UBS cutting to $14 on valuation saying a solid quarter is what analysts already expect — with i7's unhealed ~200bp take-rate decline as the quality-of-beat line; shrunk for a 14.4% short base at 5.8 days to cover and for eBay's strong 10-28 recommerce read (i2), and on a 17% implied move the direction is a lean, not a decision.
